primary_source.article: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation

findings.claim: DVS module ablation is 80% spatial-only, 88% after direction, 94% full
RGB rehabilitation reaches 90% macro-class and 62% overall subclass accuracy; spatial-only overall 43%, adding velocity 56.5%, full 62%
5-shot DVS is approximately 70% versus ResNet-50 C3D 58% and ViViT 28%; 5-shot RGB macro-class approximately 75% versus about 20% and 21%
Direction representation reports 97% classification with frame-dropout/interpolation robustness
The system is about 5M parameters versus cited 240-300M baselines and minutes versus hours of downstream training
findings.scope: This verifies what the paper reports; it is not an independent matched-hardware wall-clock or parameter-accounting reproduction.

findings.claim: Pretraining uses task-agnostic synthetic modules with 512-neuron vanilla RNNs
findings.details: The article specifies three 512-neuron RNN modules. Direction uses 100-frame moving-bar clips over 12 directions with Bernoulli noise p=0.01; velocity uses five speeds and 12 directions; salience uses drifting Gaussian-centroid dot clouds.

findings.claim: Only lightweight downstream adaptation is trained and transfer is one epoch
findings.details: The article says a small adapter/Hebbian-inspired fusion is trained at deployment and few-shot adaptation occurs in a single epoch without disrupting pretrained attractor dynamics. It also describes SVM module readouts and validation-set adaptive Hebbian fusion, so 'only an adapter' should not be expanded into a stronger claim that every downstream learned component is literally one parameter block without source-code confirmation.

findings.claim: Official code is publicly available and has been source-audited in this verification
findings.details: The primary article explicitly points to Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 for all simulation/analysis code. The current web path could not resolve the DOI/record beyond the publisher declaration, so exact files, seeds, frozen-vs-trained boundaries and reproducible commands were not inspected in this run. This is a retrieval limitation, not evidence of code absence.

scope_guards: The performance and ablation values are primary-paper verified but not independently rerun.
The parameter/time comparison is author-reported and may not be a fully matched compute/hardware comparison.
The paper's attractor-transfer results do not establish a unique neuroscience causal explanation; they demonstrate an engineered modular RNN mechanism.
Do not treat code availability as code reproduction until the Zenodo artifact is fetched and source-audited.
exact_followup: Fetch Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 through an accessible artifact path; pin file checksums/version; inspect preprocessing, RNN checkpoints, frozen/trainable boundaries, few-shot split construction, seeds and baseline accounting; reproduce the cheapest DVS ablation or direction-decoder robustness trajectory before upgrading reproducibility status.
